Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The umpires are out in the middle followed by the players of Zimbabwe. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique walk out as the openers for Pakistan. For Zimbabwe, Blessing Muzarabani will bowl the first over.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Richard Ngarava, the highest run-scorer for Zimbabwe is in for a chat. He says he is happy with the way he batted but would have loved to get to the 50. Also mentions that the team comes first. Further adds that the pitch is slightly on the slower side and if they can chip a few early wickets they will have a chance.

Pakistan's bowling started on an uncertain note, but a brilliant piece of fielding by Abdullah Shafique led to the first wicket, which sparked a turnaround in their fortunes. Debutant Faisal Akram was virtually unplayable, claiming three wickets to leave the Zimbabwean batsmen reeling. Salman Agha also impressed, taking three wickets of his own. Aamer Jamal, Mohammad Hasnain, and Haris Rauf chipped in with a wicket each, as Pakistan's bowlers eventually found their rhythm to restrict Zimbabwe. Can Zimbabwe pull off an upset and defend this or will we see yet another dominating performance with the bat from Pakistani batters? We shall have our answers soon.

Zimbabwe's innings got off to a flying start, with the hosts racing to 40 for no loss inside six overs. However, a mix-up between Joylord Gumbie and Tadiwanashe Marumani to Gumbie's dismissal, and the Zimbabwean innings began to unravel. At the 10-over mark, Zimbabwe had stumbled to 62 for 2, and the wickets continued to fall at regular intervals. The hosts struggled to gain momentum in the middle phase, and at one point, it seemed unlikely they would even reach 150, with seven wickets down for 125. However, an unlikely eighth-wicket partnership between Sikandar Raza and Richard Ngarava turned the innings around. The duo added 62 crucial runs, propelling Zimbabwe to a respectable total. Surprisingly, Richard Ngarava top-scored with a valuable 48 runs, helping the hosts post a competitive score.
We are at the mid-way break of the game and Pakistan has bundled out hosts on a mere 205. The decision of Mohammad Rizwan to put Zimbabwe first out to bat has worked in their favor.

Commentary.Commentary: All the pre-match formalities are completed, and we’re all set for the action to kick off! The two umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed by Pakistan fielders who are spreading across the field after a final pep-talk from their skipper in a close-knit huddle. Pakistan players are proudly sporting vibrant orange caps in support of KidzCan Zimbabwe, an organization dedicated to raising awareness and fighting childhood cancer. Joylord Gumbie and Tadiwanashe Marumani are the openers for Zimbabwe! Aamer Jamal has been handed the new ball and will start the proceedings for Pakistan, on debut!

The players, led by the skippers and match officials, are making their way onto the field for the national anthems. To add to the excitement, the sun is finally peeking through the clouds which is a great sign! First up will be the national anthem of Pakistan followed by that of the hosts, Zimbabwe!

Craig Ervine, the skipper of Zimbabwe says they would have wanted to bowl first as well mainly because of the overhead conditions. Adds that their preparation in the last week has been great and they look forward to the series. Mentions that the mood is great in the camp and informs that Brian Bennett and Trevor Gwandu will make their debuts.

The skipper of Pakistan, Mohammad Rizwan says they will bowl first. Adds that the first hour of the game will probably favor the bowlers hence they have decided to bowl first. Mentions that the confidence of the players is sky-high after the series win against the Aussies. Informs that they have three debutants with Haseebullah, Jamal and Faisal making their debut.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Saim Ayub, Abdullah Shafique, Irfan Khan, Mohammad Rizwan(C/WK), Haseebullah Khan (on Debut), Kamran Ghulam, Salman Agha, Aamer Jamal (on Debut), Haris Rauf, Mohammad Hasnain, Faisal Akram (on Debut).

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tadiwanashe Marumani, Joylord Gumbie (WK), Dion Myers, Craig Ervine (C), Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza, Brian Bennett (on Debut), Brandon Mavuta, Blessing Muzarabani, Trevor Gwandu (on Debut), Richard Ngarava.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the coin flip and they have decided to BOWL first!

UPDATE - 7.02 am GMT - Great news! The covers are off, and the weather seems to be taking a turn for the better. While it’s still a bit gloomy, it doesn’t look like it’ll hold up proceedings. The stumps are up, and the players are out on the field, getting warmed up. The toss is just around the corner, so don’t go anywhere – the action is about to begin!

UPDATE - The weather isn't looking too promising, with overcast skies expected to linger for the next couple of hours. At the moment, it's a gloomy scene with a light drizzle and the covers remain firmly in place. Fingers crossed this clears up soon so we can gear up for the toss and get the game underway! On a brighter note, Pakistan have announced their playing XI, featuring three debutants ready to make their mark. Haseebullah Khan, Aamer Jamal and Faisal Akram will be stepping onto the field for their maiden ODI appearance! Stay tuned for more updates!

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, will be led by Craig Ervine and will be looking to make a strong impression against a depleted Pakistani side. The hosts have made some interesting additions to their squad, including three players who are yet to make their ODI debut for the national team. With a mix of experience and youth, Zimbabwe hopes to catch Pakistan off guard and secure a winning start to the series. Can Pakistan continue their dominance over the hosts or will Zimbabwe pull off an upset? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Pakistan, led by new skipper Mohammad Rizwan, will be brimming with confidence after their impressive 2-1 victory against the Aussies in their recent tour to Australia. However, they will be without the services of some of their key players, including Babar Azam, Naseem Shah, and Shaheen Afridi, who have been rested for the series.

Hello and welcome to everybody tuning in! The 1st ODI of the three-match series between Zimbabwe and Pakistan is set to get underway, marking the beginning of an exciting contest between the two teams. Queens Sports Club, Bulawayo will host this contest.
... MATCHDAY ...

The stacked international cricketing calendar of 2024 seems to be ending the year with a whole host of series all across the globe and now, Zimbabwe welcome Pakistan for a three-match ODI series followed by a T20I series as well. The first ODI will be played at the Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo as both sides get into the groove for ODI action, Pakistan more so as they continue their preparation for the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy in a couple of months time or so. Zimbabwe haven't faced a full member nation in white-ball cricket since they welcomed India a fair few months ago in July but they have been playing competitive cricket in the ICC T20 World Cup, Sub Regional African Qualifiers, Group B and they demolished every opponent in their path. Their squad also includes as many as three uncapped players for this upcoming series but all eyes will be on the likes of skipper Craig Ervine along with the likes of Sikandar Raza and Sean Williams. They have more than a decent pace attack featuring the likes of Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava but it still needs a bit more oomph and the batting too seems a bit undercooked if you take out 2-3 players. Pakistan on the other hand are fresh off their superb ODI series win in Australia against the hosts where they came back from 1-0 down to match the series. Most of the core team that featured in Australia has been retained but there's no Babar Azam or even the pace duo of Naseem Shah and Shaheen Afridi for that matter. Mohammad Rizwan will continue to lead the side featuring the likes of Saim Ayub, Haris Rauf and Irfan Khan who have done well in recent times but overall, it is a fairly inexperienced side filled with budding talent. They will be confident even after being clean swept in the T20I series against the Aussies as they did win the ODI series and will be expected to gun for another away series win with a probable home ICC Champions Trophy on the horizon. Who are you backing to take the lead in the series?
